title: Daycare expansion approved at Erb Street West
subtitle: Strategic plan scan report, new Microsoft agreement, City Centre lease renewal and Dog Designation Appeal Committee appointment.
overview: Council approved a zoning amendment that lets the Waterloo Infant Toddler Daycare Association use the whole of an existing building at 372 Erb Street West as a child care centre {{vote:m7}}. The change adds child care space in Ward 6, and councillors noted the site is on a transit line and is walkable. One councillor declared a conflict and did not take part in the vote.

Council also received the draft scan report for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan as information {{vote:m4}}. It summarizes engagement from November to February. Staff said the draft plan will come to Council on May 8, with final approval planned for June 26.

Council approved a new three-year Microsoft enterprise agreement {{vote:m5}} and a lease renewal for a space at the Waterloo City Centre {{vote:m6}}. It also appointed a member to the Dog Designation Appeal Committee {{vote:m3}}.
Council met in closed session earlier in the afternoon on appointments, a possible land disposition and labour relations. The minutes report no decisions from that session.

decisions.item: Zoning amendment for 372 Erb Street West
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-02 so the Waterloo Infant Toddler Daycare Association can operate a child care centre in the whole of the existing building and the front yard setback is legalized.
Council received report CAO2023-015 on the scan and engagement work for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan as information.
Council approved a new three-year agreement between Microsoft, CDW Canada and the City, and authorized the Mayor and City Clerk to sign it.
Council approved renewing the lease for space at the Waterloo City Centre held by the local Member of Provincial Parliament, on the terms in report COM2023-008.
Council approved report CORP2023-019 and enacted a by-law appointing Christopher Mallick to the Dog Designation Appeal Committee.

debate: On the daycare site, one councillor asked whether the added parking was needed and whether the space could go to green space or the playground. Staff said the zoning sets a minimum parking rate and the existing child care centre's parking is fully used, though the front yard could be redesigned later.

A councillor asked about housing above the child care centre. Staff said the zoning already allows residential on upper floors, but the lot is too small for that without redeveloping. The applicant's representative said advancing this use separately was more efficient because of time limits tied to federal funding. The two adjacent sites might be linked later.

On the strategic plan, councillors asked how advisory committees and equity-deserving groups can respond to the draft given the tight timeline. Staff said participants will be notified when the May agenda is published, but staff cannot attend every advisory committee.

Several councillors urged that arts and culture be built into the strategic plan. They noted it was named a strength in the scan but not listed among opportunities. They cited its economic value, its role in attracting talent and the need for arts-ready spaces.
Councillors welcomed the Microsoft agreement as a way to reduce costs over time and move the City toward a more unified technology approach.
